pub_title: Profiling people with Parkinson's disease at risk of cognitive decline: Insights from PPMI and ICICLE‐PD data
dataset_context_from_paper: Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) data were used, accessed on November 15, 2022. PPMI is an international, observational, cohort study with almost 50 sites across 13 countries. Eligibility was contingent on a diagnosis of PD no longer than 2 years prior to enrolment and drug naïve status. Participants with young-onset PD (age < 50) and dementia were excluded. Data were available annually from baseline up to year 7. Participants with two or more data points were included, resulting in N= 770 baseline participants. Latent class mixed models were created to identify subgroups with similar longitudinal cognitive trajectories using total MoCA score as the outcome variable.
dataset_keywords: Parkinson's disease, cognitive decline, longitudinal cohort

pub_title: Profiling people with Parkinson's disease at risk of cognitive decline: Insights from PPMI and ICICLE‐PD data
dataset_context_from_paper: Incidence of Cognitive Impairment in Cohorts with Longitudinal Evaluation-Parkinson's Disease (ICICLE-PD) data were used, accessed on October 10, 2022. ICICLE-PD was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and GCP guidelines. Recruitment for ICICLE-PD took place from the community in Cambridgeshire and Newcastle upon Tyne/Gateshead, United Kingdom. All participants were recently diagnosed people with PD meeting Queen's Square Brain Bank Criteria, with working knowledge of English and no significant baseline cognitive impairment. Data were available every 18-months from baseline to year 4.5. Participants with two or more data points were included, resulting in N= 212 baseline participants. Latent class mixed models were applied to identify cognitive subtypes based on rate of decline in Montreal Cognitive Assessment.
dataset_keywords: Parkinson's disease, cognitive impairment, dementia risk

pub_title: Eight weeks of creatine monohydrate supplementation is associated with increased muscle strength and size in Alzheimer’s disease: data from a single-arm pilot study
dataset_context_from_paper: This single-arm pilot trial, conducted at the University of Kansas Medical Center in Kansas City, examined the intervention-associated changes in muscle strength, muscle size, and neuromuscular junction (NMJ) integrity following 8 weeks of CrM supplementation (20 g/day) in 20 participants with AD. All participants completed handgrip-strength measurements on the dominant hand, with ten participants completing lower body strength assessment via leg dynamometry at three velocities, eighteen participants completing muscle size assessment by ultrasound measurement, and nineteen participants completing NMJ integrity assessment by measuring plasma C-terminal agrin fragment (CAF) levels. dataset_keywords: Alzheimer's disease, creatine supplementation, muscle strength

dataset_context_from_paper: RNA sequencing data from the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) of individuals with severe Alzheimer's disease and healthy controls. The dataset was originally deposited by Scheckel et al. (2016) and derived from frozen brain tissues classified based on the Consortium to Establish a Registry for Alzheimer's Disease (CERAD) criteria. The original study included eight control subjects and nine patients with advanced or severe AD (CDR 4-5), matched for age and sex with brief postmortem intervals. The authors filtered and selected four controls and six advanced AD samples for downstream analysis using next-generation knowledge discovery methods. RNA was extracted using the TRIzol method and sequenced using an Illumina HiSeq 2500. The dataset was analyzed using GEO2R to identify 24,207 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) at P ≤0.05, further filtered to 3,103 genes using a fold change cut-off of ±1.5. WebGestalt and Ingenuity Pathway Analysis were used to identify dysregulated pathways including retrograde endocannabinoid signaling, motor proteins, oxidative phosphorylation, ribosome biogenesis, immune system activation, antigen processing and presentation, and cytokine signaling in severe AD.
